dimensions.rationale: Every destination-file construction from a tainted entry name is now canonicalized and containment-checked, so the whole Zip Slip class (not just `../`) is closed.
dimensions.evidence: ZipUtil.java: `resolveDestinationFile(outputDir, name)` replaces `new File(outputDir, name)` at Unpacker.process (~1152), BackslashUnpacker.process both branches (~1244/1252) and its mkdir loop, and Unwraper.process (~1290); helper does `outputDir.getCanonicalPath()` / `file.getCanonicalPath()` then `!filePath.equals(outputDirPath) && !filePath.startsWith(outputDirPath + File.separator)` → ZipException.

dimensions.rationale: Guard is placed at the sink (destination resolution) rather than at a caller or on the raw entry string, so all entry-name shapes are neutralized where the path becomes a File.
dimensions.evidence: Private static helper `resolveDestinationFile(File outputDir, String name)` interposed at each `new File(outputDir, name)` sink; no reliance on `name.indexOf("..")` blocklisting (unlike the official fix).

Verified Zips.java:471/unpack paths route through ZipUtil.

dimensions.label: Mitigation soundness

issues.description: No execution evidence at all: pov_before_reproduced=false (the POV never demonstrated the vulnerability pre-patch), pov_after_present=false, and regressions_ran=0/regressions_passed=null. The verdict rests entirely on static review; I confirmed by reading the checked-out source that the patch compiles (ZipException is unchecked, ZipExceptionUtil.rethrow exists, BackslashUnpacker is public, all test imports present) and that existing tests such as ZipUtilTest:878 remain satisfied, but nothing was actually executed. This is an evidence gap, not an identified defect.

BackslashUnpacker's directory loop now validates each segment against its immediate parent, so an archive containing an intermediate traversal segment that nets back inside outputDir (e.g. `a\..\b.txt`) is rejected, whereas the official fix only checks the final destFile and would allow it. Stricter than upstream; essentially no realistic legitimate archive is affected.

resolveDestinationFile calls getCanonicalPath() on both outputDir and the destination for every entry (and for every path segment in BackslashUnpacker), whereas the official fix short-circuits unless the name contains "..". This adds two filesystem syscalls per entry — a measurable but minor throughput cost on very large archives. It is the price of closing the non-".." bypass class, so the trade is favourable.

Residual TOCTOU: the canonical-path check happens before FileUtils.forceMkdir/FileUtils.copy, so an attacker able to swap a component for a symlink concurrently with extraction could still redirect a write. Inherent to this design and identical to the official fix; not a regression introduced by this patch.

result.root_cause: ZipUtil resolved attacker-controlled ZIP entry names directly against the extraction directory (`new File(outputDir, name)`) in Unpacker.process, BackslashUnpacker.process, and Unwraper.process without verifying that the resulting canonical path stays inside outputDir, letting a crafted entry name write files anywhere the JVM has permission ("Zip Slip").
result.summary: This is a good fix and a strict superset of the official one. It interposes a single `resolveDestinationFile` helper at every tainted sink — all three `new File(outputDir, name)` sites confirmed by grep over src/main, plus the BackslashUnpacker mkdir loop the upstream fix left unguarded — and applies the CWE-022 defense-of-record: canonicalize both sides, then require the destination to equal outputDir or start with `outputDir + File.separator`, failing closed with ZipException. Dropping the official's `name.indexOf("..")` gate and adding the separator boundary closes two bypasses upstream left open (non-`..` symlink/canonicalization escapes, and prefix-sibling directories like /tmp/outEvil matching /tmp/out via bare startsWith). The one real weakness is verification, not code: the pipeline reproduced no POV before the patch and ran zero regression tests, so I set the no_regressions gate false on missing evidence — static review of the actual checkout (unchecked ZipException, ZipExceptionUtil.rethrow, public BackslashUnpacker, existing test imports) found no compile or behavioral breakage.
